Article Title: 'We are going to destroy BJP': Rahul Gandhi's big declaration as opposition sits in to protest against CEC
Article Text:
'We are not only countering them, we are going to destroy them'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday questioned the Delhi Police over "stopping and threatening" INDIA bloc MPs who were marching to the Election Commission , saying the Opposition wanted to question Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged "vote chori".In a social media post, Rahul said the Election Commissioners were not meeting the Opposition MPs despite their reques"More than 300 opposition MPs marched from Parliament to the Election Commission today to meet the Election Commissioners," the Congress leader said."We represent crores of Indians. Why aren't the Election Commissioners meeting us? Why is the police stopping and threatening us?" he asked.Later, when asked about the BJP's allegation that he was misleading people on the issue, Rahul said he was not concerned about what the BJP said and asserted that he was not merely countering the party but "destroying" it."We are not only countering them, we are going to destroy them. I have no interest in what BJP says. I am standing here to save the democracy of India. A few hours ago, 300 Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs came here with me. They too are trying to save democracy in the country," Rahul said."Amit Shah, Narendra Modi, Mohan Bhagwat and Gyanesh Kumar... these people have destroyed the country's democratic system. The entire country believes this.The youth of the country believe and understand this. Even the policemen who were stopping me here just now were saying the same thing," he added.Rahul alleged that the country had been "hijacked" through "vote theft", accusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of being responsible."The country has been hijacked by Narendra Modi through vote theft. Amit Shah has hijacked it. Mohan Bhagwat has hijacked it, and Gyanesh Kumar has helped them. You will see... I am saying this after careful consideration. Action will be taken against all of them. You will see, not a single one of them will escape. Whether it is Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Gyanesh Kumar or Mohan Bhagwat," he said."What has been done to our country, is called treason. Nobody is going to escape," Rahul added.The remarks came after Rahul, along with INDIA bloc MPs, staged a sit-in metres away from the Election Commission of India's (ECI) office at the Akashvani Bhawan premises.Rahul, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal, MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Pawan Khera and Imran Pratapgarhi were seen sitting under a tree after Opposition leaders pushed open the gates of the Akashvani Bhawan premises in an attempt to reach the ECI headquarters, located around 300 metres away.According to sources, a PCR call was later made from Akashvani Bhawan, alleging that Rahul had entered the premises forcibly.Addressing reporters, Congress leader Pawan Khera said, "The Election Commission is right next to us, and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha is not being allowed to go to the Election Commission; he has been stopped. So, you can see Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, our Venugopal, Channi, Imran Pratapgarhi and all of us are sitting in protest here inside Akashvani Bhawan.""The Election Commission is barely 100 metres from here, and when the Leader of Opposition wants to go there and submit a memorandum, he is being stopped, and everyone is being stopped very harshly. You saw the situation outside. This is the state of democracy in the national capital of this country," he added.Carrying tricolours and banners reading "Save democracy", INDIA bloc MPs raised slogans against the CEC, BJP and RSS as they marched towards the ECI headquarters. Delhi Police and other security forces were placed on alert in view of the protest, while barricades were erected outside the ECI office.Rahul and Priyanka, along with several other INDIA bloc leaders, were also briefly detained after they were stopped from proceeding towards the ECI office.Rahul was stopped by multiple layers of police barricades while attempting to reach the ECI headquarters. He subsequently climbed onto one of the barricades and waved a large national flag, drawing loud slogans of support from INDIA bloc leaders and workers gathered at the spot.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi questions Delhi Police over "stopping and threatening" Opposition MPs. Opposition wanted to question Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged "vote chori" Rahul alleged that the country had been "hijacked" through "vote theft"

Article Title: 'Wanted to tarnish image': Delhi Police on man held over alleged AI poster showing cop sexually assaulting woman
Article Text:
Police said Nadeem admitted during questioning that he used AI tools to create such videos. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Tuesday said 24-year-old Nadeem Ahmed , arrested for allegedly creating and circulating an AI-generated fake poster falsely depicting a police officer sexually assaulting a woman during a protest, made it “to tarnish the image of the police and turn protesters against them. ”Addressing a press conference, additional deputy commissioner of Police (New Delhi) Manjeet said Nadeem admitted during questioning that he used AI tools to create such videos.Police said Nadeem claimed to be an independent journalist and had been running an Instagram account since April. The account had around 24,000 followers and 1,226 posts, according to investigators.“On 3rd October, we saw a footage circulating on social media wherein it is being shown as the CCTV footage from the protest site. It is being portrayed that an individual in Police uniform is misbehaving with a woman. Through social media, the identity of the officer is being revealed. When we examined it, we found that one Nadeem Ahmed, a r/o Palwal, Haryana was running that channel. We arrested him. In the initial questioning, he told us that he is an independent journalist. He told us that he had studied till class 10 in Madrasa of Saket, Delhi,” police said.“He also told us that he is a 10th-fail. Upon further questioning, he told us that he has AI tools, with the help of which he keeps making such videos. When we asked him why he made such videos, he told us that he wanted to tarnish the image of Police so that the protesters coming there would start harbouring hatred for the Police and start attacking them. We took immediate cognisance of this and arrested him. We will take him into police remand and further question him. His source of funding and accomplices are matters of investigation. We have seized his phone for further analysis. He became more active during CJP protest. So, we will analyse if this is part of any bigger conspiracy...” police added.Nadeem, who studied at a madrassa in Saket and failed to clear Class 10, was arrested on Monday and produced before a court, which granted police custody for further investigation.Police are also investigating whether others were involved in the alleged conspiracy and are working to identify them. His phone has been seized for forensic and further analysis.The arrest comes amid a controversy over an assistant commissioner of police accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.ACP Vivek Bhagat was promoted to the rank of additional deputy commissioner on Monday along with three other officers from his batch. However, the order assigning him additional charge was withdrawn on Tuesday.According to the government, Bhagat requested "of his own volition" not to take charge until a full inquiry into the alleged harassment of women journalists is conducted and "satisfactorily concluded".Earlier, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das had accused Delhi Police of refusing to register an FIR against an additional DCP over an alleged assault on an independent journalist and demanded action against the officer. Separately, complaints by three women journalists alleging harassment by police personnel had triggered protests and demands for action.
Article Summary: Police said Nadeem claimed to be an independent journalist and had been running an Instagram account since April. The account had around 24,000 followers and 1,226 posts, according to investigators. Police are also investigating whether others were involved in the alleged conspiracy and are working to identify them.

Article Title: 'Acted of his own volition': ACP Bhagat steps aside from Addl DCP charge amid harassment probe
Article Text:
Amid harassment probe, ACP Bhagat steps aside from Addl DCP charge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Connaught Place Vivek Bhagat, who was promoted to the rank of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Addl DCP), has sought withdrawal of the order assigning him the post, citing an ongoing inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment.Following his request to step aside pending the inquiry, the Delhi government modified its administrative order assigning the current duty charge of Addl DCP to 12 Selection Grade DANIPS officers.Earlier, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu had approved assigning the current duty charge (CDC) of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police to 12 DANIPS officers posted with the Delhi Police with immediate effect. ACP Vivek Bhagat, who is currently serving as SDPO Connaught Place, was among the officers named in the order.The Delhi government later issued a clarification saying the October 5 order was being amended following a formal request from Bhagat."Vivek Bhagat, ACP, of his own volition, has requested not to avail the current duty charge assignment, till a full enquiry has been conducted in the matter of alleged harassment of women journalists and such enquiry has been satisfactorily concluded. Accordingly, the order dated October 5, 2026, as aforesaid, is being modified and will be reissued with respect to assignment of current duty charge on the eleven remaining officers," the Delhi government stated in a post on X.The administration clarified that the assignment is an interim administrative arrangement and does not amount to a regular promotion."As stated in the order, the assignment of current duty charge is a temporary arrangement which confers no financial benefit, and no statutory duties of the regular incumbents can be exercised by the officers to whom current duty charge has been assigned," the statement added.Following Bhagat’s exclusion, a revised order assigning the current duty charge to the remaining 11 DANIPS officers will be issued shortly.Earlier in the day, Bhagat, who has been accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during the October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar, was included in the order assigning the rank of Additional DCP, drawing criticism from various quarters.Three women journalists had accused Delhi Police personnel of sexual harassment during the October 3 protest against alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Delhi Police has received the complaints and forwarded them to the Crime Branch for further inquiry.
Article Summary: Vivek Bhagat, who was promoted to the rank of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Addl DCP), has sought withdrawal of the order assigning him the post. He has been accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during the October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar. The Delhi government later issued a clarification saying the October 5 order was being amended following a formal request.

Article Title: 'Largely irrelevant': Jaishankar says UN failing on Gulf, Ukraine, Africa and Covid
Article Text:
File photo: EAM Jaishankar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has called the United Nations “largely irrelevant” to decision-making on major global crises, blaming a “gridlocked” Security Council and its outdated composition for the organisation’s ineffectiveness.Speaking at the fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi on Monday, Jaishankar said the UN had struggled to play a meaningful role in addressing major international issues, including conflicts in the Gulf and Ukraine, crises in Africa and the Covid-19 pandemic.“Where the UN is concerned, I think it's obvious to everybody by now that the UN is gridlocked,” Jaishankar said.“If you look at the big issues of the day... actually, the United Nations has been largely irrelevant to the decision-making,” he added.Jaishankar said much of the problem stemmed from the Security Council’s inability to reach decisions. He also questioned whether its current composition reflected the wider international community.The UN was founded with 51 members and now has almost four times that number, he noted.“So, if you have grown four times, and you want to keep the old board of management, it's not going to work. I mean, it's common sense,” he said.Jaishankar also criticised countries that he said were resisting UN reform while citing Africa’s interests as a reason.He said Africa had already presented a clear position during intergovernmental negotiations on what it wanted from reform of the world body.Despite his criticism, Jaishankar said the answer was not to bypass the UN.“We need the UN. The UN has done a big service to the international community,” he said.“Our job must be to ‘fix the UN, not to work around the UN’,” he added, saying the UN itself needed to contribute to the reform process.India has been pushing for comprehensive UN reforms, including expansion of the Security Council. It has worked with the G4 grouping of India, Japan, Brazil and Germany, as well as the L.69 group of developing countries, to build support for reform.Jaishankar has previously criticised the UN’s structure, saying the organisation had failed to keep pace with a world that had become more interconnected and multipolar.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar says the UN has struggled to play a meaningful role in addressing major international issues. He blames a “gridlocked” Security Council and its outdated composition for the organisation’s ineffectiveness. India has been pushing for comprehensive UN reforms, including expansion of Security Council.

Article Title: Abhijeet Dipke claims CJP activists receiving police notices threatening October 10 protest 'could turn violent'
Article Text:
‘One nation, one political party’: Abhijeet Dipke targets Centre, alleges pressure on CJP activists

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday targeted the centre and alleged that “One Nation, One Election” was merely a slogan and alleged that the government’s intention was to establish “one nation, one political party”.He also claimed that activists of the Cockroach Janta Party were being served police notices and pressured against participating in protests."I have said multiple times that the Maharashtra Police is the best police force in the country, and the Delhi Police should learn from them. But it is heartbreaking that the Chandrapur police served notices to CJP workers, telling them not to participate in the agitation at Jantar Mantar. They also asked about the source of the expenses for travelling to Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.Dipke questioned how police could predict that the agitation would turn violent. He also questioned the police directive to CJP activists against making social media posts that could allegedly lead to violence."We speak about (Mahatma) Gandhi and B R Ambedkar. Do they think it is violent?" he asked.The CJP had earlier welcomed the INDIA bloc’s proposed protest on Tuesday, saying its own October 10 mobilisation should be seen as a broader call by the youth rather than an event led by any particular organisation.CJP co-convener Saurav Das said everyone, including political parties, student organisations, activists and members of the public, should assert their rights through peaceful protests.CJP co-convener Saurav Das said the organisation welcomed the INDIA bloc’s planned protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Tuesday.“We welcome all peaceful protests. Everyone should make efforts, be it INDIA bloc or other student organisations or activists, or common people. Everyone needs to assert their rights,” Das told a press conference.Das said repeated protests indicated that people were not being heard. “If people are hitting the streets repeatedly then there is a problem,” he said, adding that taking to the streets was the “last resort” for people who felt their concerns were not being addressed.At the press conference, Das also claimed that the CJP had received information from “well-wishers” within the establishment that its leaders could be arrested ahead of the October 10 protest. “Well wishers have informed us that meetings are taking place and there is a high possibility that CJP leaders could be arrested,” he claimed. “It does not matter if we are arrested or detained because this fight is about the young generation.“Even if we are arrested or detained the protest will go on because this is the fight for our future,” he asserted. “Fear of FIR, fear of jail has evaporated -- it won't work anymore.”Das said Jantar Mantar had become a “symbol of hope and victory” and asserted that protesters would sit wherever police stopped them. “Wherever police stops us, we will sit there and that will become Jantar Mantar,” he said.Das also referred to the Supreme Court’s Monday remarks on the controversy surrounding Form 6, accusing the Election Commission of misrepresenting the court’s position. “The EC sought to clarify in its press statement that the Supreme Court upheld changes in Form 6. Today, the Supreme Court has said the EC lied,” he said.Chief Justice Surya Kant, during a hearing on Monday, said the Supreme Court had not approved any modification to Form 6. The clarification assumes significance as the EC, in its September 26 statement following a meeting of the full commission, had said the “declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court”.On the CJP’s October 10 mobilisation, Das said the protest should be viewed as a broader youth movement rather than the initiative of a particular organisation. “You should not consider the call for protests on October 10 as our call or someone else's call. This is the call by the youth and Gen Z. We are one part of that.”His remarks came against the backdrop of an online exchange over the weekend between the CJP and sections aligned with the Congress, after a social media post compared CJP national convener Abhijeet Dipke with AISA president Neha Bora. Dipke and Bora rejected any suggestion of rivalry, while CJP leaders accused sections of the “liberal ecosystem” of attempting to undermine Dipke.AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj also weighed in, cautioning against replacing one form of “hero worship” with another.The exchange brought differences between the CJP and sections of the Congress into the open. Some Congress leaders have been wary of the CJP’s emergence, given the AAP background of several of its prominent faces, while the AAP has backed its recent mobilisations.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleges that ‘One Nation, One Election’ was merely a slogan. He also claimed that activists of the Cockroach Janta Party were being served police notices and pressured against participating in protests. CJP co- convener Saurav Das said everyone, including political parties, student organisations, activists and members of the public, should assert their rights through peaceful protests.

Article Title: 'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, time to resign': Rahul Gandhi as INDIA bloc march to EC stopped
Article Text:
'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, Time to resign,' Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X

INDIA bloc MPs stopped near Niti Aayog

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday called on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign as INDIA bloc MPs marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission of India headquarters over alleged discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, Time to resign,” Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X as he led the opposition MPs towards the ECI office.The march, which began from Parliament's Makar Dwar around 11 am, was stopped by security personnel near the Niti Aayog office. Several INDIA bloc MPs subsequently sat in protest, with opposition leaders later staging a dharna at Parliament Street.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule were among the opposition leaders participating in the march.Visuals showed Rahul Gandhi leading the march along with several INDIA bloc MPs, who were carrying placards and cutouts of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The opposition MPs were seeking Kumar's removal over alleged irregularities in the SIR process. The INDIA bloc had announced the march from Parliament to Nirvachan Sadan as part of its campaign against the Election Commission's handling of the electoral roll revision.The march was met with heavy security deployment in central Delhi. Barricades were placed along the route and Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed around Transport Bhawan ahead of the protest.After being prevented from proceeding towards the ECI headquarters, several opposition MPs sat in protest near Parliament Street.AAP said it would skip the march, with the party saying it would fight the issue through its own means.Opposition steps up attack over SIRThe protest comes amid an ongoing political confrontation between the opposition and the Election Commission over the SIR exercise and alleged discrepancies in voter rolls.The Supreme Court on Tuesday said it had not approved any modified version of Form 6 used for voter enrolment during the SIR process. CJI Surya Kant said, “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us.”The court issued notices to the Centre, ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and other officials while declining to pass an ex-parte interim order suspending Kumar.Ahead of the march, several opposition leaders criticised the Election Commission's handling of the SIR process. Congress and INDIA bloc leaders have demanded Kumar's removal, while the BJP has rejected the opposition's allegations.Mamata Banerjee has said the protests will continue until Kumar resigns and has also demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation.Congress MP Jairam Ramesh had said the march would be peaceful. The opposition has also announced district-level padyatras till October 8 and "Save votes, save the country" rallies from October 25 to November 25.
Article Summary: 'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, Time to resign,' Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X as he led the opposition MPs towards the ECI office. The march, which began from Parliament's Makar Dwar around 11 am, was stopped by security personnel near the Niti Aayog office.

Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 9

Rank Nation Gold Silver Bronze Total 1 China 132 53 45 230 2 Japan 41 68 63 172 3 South Korea 21 26 43 90 4 Uzbekistan 12 17 13 42 5 Kazakhstan 9 13 23 45 6 Thailand 9 8 13 30 7 Bahrain 9 2 3 14 8 Iran 8 15 9 32 9 North Korea 7 5 5 17 10 Malaysia 6 3 9 18 11 Hong Kong 5 12 17 34 12 INDIA 4 20 21 45

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

NEW DELHI: Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) chief and MLA Humayun Kabir was briefly detained by Rejinagar Police and taken away from his party office in Murshidabad on Tuesday following a heated argument with police.The detention came after he cast his vote in the Rejinagar Assembly constituency by-election.Voting began early Tuesday for by-elections to five Assembly seats across West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, along with a Lok Sabha seat in Assam.In West Bengal, polling is being held in the Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly constituencies. The Nandigram seat fell vacant after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari won from two constituencies in the state Assembly elections earlier this year and chose to retain the other seat.The Rejinagar seat fell vacant after Kabir, who had won from both Rejinagar and Nowda, resigned from one of the constituencies.The Rejinagar contest includes BJP nominee Sakharav Sarkar, former Murshidabad district president; Mamata Banerjee-led TMC candidate Rabiul Alam Chowdhury; rival TMC candidate Safiuzzaman Sheikh; Congress nominee Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi; and CPI(M)'s Syed Asad Ali.The administration has put in place multi-layered security arrangements to maintain law and order and ensure peaceful polling, officials said.Rejinagar has 2.57 lakh electors and 315 polling stations, while Nandigram has 2.67 lakh voters and 323 polling stations. Webcasting is available at all polling booths in both constituencies.Counting of votes will take place on October 9.

NEW DELHI: The Punjab government will approach the Supreme Court to challenge the Punjab and Haryana high court’s order directing a CBI probe into the matter concerning three letters written by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the Punjab Director General of Police (DGP), AAP said.The state government will file an appeal against the High Court’s order.The High Court had on Monday directed that the matter be handed over to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) after hearing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by advocate Nikhil Thamman. The petition was filed after the Punjab Police allegedly failed to register a case based on the ED’s letters.The ED had sought registration of an FIR against Rajbir Singh Ghumman, Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, and certain other individuals over alleged corruption.During the hearing, Thamman also submitted that Punjab has not had a regular DGP for more than four years. The petition referred to the Supreme Court’s judgment in the Prakash Singh vs Union of India case and its directions on the appointment of a regular DGP from a panel recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).Meanwhile, Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh alleged systemic corruption in the state administration and warned officials against aligning with the government following the High Court’s order to transfer the matter to the CBI.Speaking to ANI, Singh criticised the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), calling the party and its members a “sham” and alleging that even the office of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has come under scrutiny."This party was created by the BJP as their own B-team, but the idea was to make the laws so strict that no matter who the minister or senior official was, anyone involved in corruption would automatically end up in jail. Today, that is the situation. The entire episode involving Arvind Kejriwal and his associates is a sham. Even the Chief Minister's Office has been linked to allegations of corruption, which had also been raised earlier by the Enforcement Directorate," he said.

NEW DELHI: BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra on Tuesday accused Rahul Gandhi of misleading the public over Form 6. He alleged that the Congress and INDIA bloc were attempting to undermine constitutional institutions amid their planned protest against the Election Commission .Patra said the Supreme Court had not declared Form 6 illegal and had only agreed to examine allegations concerning changes to the form. He also rejected Gandhi's claim of differences within the Election Commission over the issue, citing an ECI fact-check that said the Bihar SIR order was approved unanimously."Rahul Gandhi posted today regarding Form 6 after the hearing in the Supreme Court on the PIL. This is an attack on the Election Commission, but the second line mentions the BJP as well, so the BJP will respond to it. Rahul Gandhi has misled the public on two points," Patra said."First, he claimed that Form 6 was illegal and specifically mentioned the Bharatiya Janata Party in this context. But the court did not declare Form 6 illegal today. The court noted that the petition mentioned changes to Form 6, so the court said it would examine the matter. We had not consented to any such changes. If any change has indeed been made, it will only become clear after the notice is issued," he said."Even after that, when we read the detailed order and look at the Election Commission's press release... it becomes clear that the Commission had explicitly stated that there was no change in Form 6, and the Supreme Court had upheld the associated declaration. Article Title: 'Beyond limits': Ex-CJI Gavai, former judges slam SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks amid EC-SIR row

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission.Gavai said that a sitting judge should not have made comments on the ongoing row over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls as the matter is sub judice before the top court."Judicial propriety would not permit him to make any comment on the matter which is sub judice before the court," Gavai told news agency PTI.Retired Delhi high court judges SN Dhingra and RS Sodhi also questioned Bhuyan's remarks.Justice Dhingra said Bhuyan's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" and such comments should not be made at a public event when the issue is pending before the same court."He should have thought a thousand times before making such a statement," Dhingra said, adding that Justice Bhuyan did not know the full facts of the issue.Justice R S Sodhi also criticised Justice Bhuyan for calling the SIR exercise disenfranchisement and said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework."Whether you have a vote or you don't have a vote depends upon the statute. If you fall within the parameters of the statute, you have a vote.If you don't fall within the parameters of the statute, you don't have a vote," Justice Sodhi said."I mean, these hardline thinking and these hardline statements, to my mind, are not a very mature way of looking at a thing, especially when you are supposed to be in a field which is supposed to be excellent in its rationalising," he said.This comes a day after Justice Bhuyan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary" and a "negation" of the constitutional order.While delivering the valedictory address at the 19th Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Justice Bhuyan said that the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and the other without voting rights, and no amount of "whataboutery" could justify such a process.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,” Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.“No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,” he said.This is not the first time that Justice Bhuyan has put forth his views on issues being discussed in the public domain.Recently, NALSAR Hyderabad was in the news after a section of its students wrote to the vice chancellor, registrar and professors of the institution, opposing any proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as chief guest to the varsity's convocation.Justice Bhuyan, who served as the Chancellor of NALSAR, on Sunday said he can be legitimately proud of the students of the institution."You have shown to the country and the world what a university student, that too, a student of law, should be like. You are brilliant. You are bold and you are brave," he said.

NEW DELHI: The ruling BJP on Monday said the Supreme Court's decision to issue notices to the Election Commission (EC) and the Centre on pleas seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar showed that all institutions in the country were "functioning independently" and there was no atmosphere of "fear and dictatorship"."The country is moving in a very democratic way. Everyone is speaking their heart out. All procedures and systems are being followed. Where else could there be a better model of democracy? I feel India is celebrating democracy," BJP MP and spokesperson Sambit Patra told reporters at a news conference at the party headquarters in Delhi when asked about the development.Patra's remarks came after the Supreme Court sought responses from the EC and the Centre within a week on a plea challenging the manner in which the poll panel, led by CEC Gyanesh Kumar, allegedly took decisions without the approval of the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.However, a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to pass any interim order in the matter.The bench observed that it could not pass an order merely on the basis of a media report, which may or may not be accurate. However, it asserted that if any decisions of the EC were found to have been taken unilaterally by the CEC, the Supreme Court could reconsider or recall them."They (EC) are expected to take unanimous decisions. If there is no unanimity, it has to be by majority. If records show some decision was not unanimous, etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra vires. Can we ex parte come to a decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," the CJI said.The controversy stems from an Indian Express report published late last month, which claimed that Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The report alleged that some of these decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.According to the report, the poll panel's ECINet software added a requirement for ancestral details and a link to the previous SIR in Form 6, the voter registration form, without the legal amendment required under election rules. The two commissioners reportedly objected to the change.The EC has since restored Form 6 to its original format in states where the SIR has been completed. However, the requirement continues in states and Union territories where the roll revision is still underway.Responding to the Indian Express report, the commission said that "differing views and observations" among its members were a "normal part" of deliberations in any multi-member institution. The EC also stated that all decisions, including those related to the SIR, were taken unanimously by Kumar and the two Election Commissioners.Meanwhile, Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi upped the ante against Kumar after the Supreme Court clarified that it did not approve any modification made by the EC in Form 6.In a social media post on X, the Congress leader accused the CEC of changing the application citizens use to register as new electors "illegally and unilaterally.""It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP," Rahul Gandhi wrote on X, adding that was now established "beyond doubt" that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 "illegally and unilaterally."He also shared the screenshot of the September 26 Election Commission statement which read -- "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used."
Article Summary: The Supreme Court issued notices to the Election Commission and the Centre on pleas seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to pass any interim order in the matter.

Article Title: Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies

NEW DELHI: Chirag Paswan once described himself as Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "Hanuman". Six years later, the LJP (Ram Vilas) chief offered another approach of his politics: "I can stand up to my government . .. I am in the alliance but I am not the BJP."This distinction becomes relevant as he prepares to take his party into the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election. LJP(RV) has announced that it will contest the polls and is preparing for all 403 constituencies, while leaving open whether it will eventually contest alone or as part of an alliance.The UP move comes after a significant change in Chirag Paswan's political position. In 2020, the undivided LJP broke with the NDA in Bihar, contested 135 seats and targeted Nitish Kumar's JD(U), while maintaining its support for PM Modi. Its slogan captured the strategy: "Modi se bair nahi, Nitish teri khair nahi." The party won only one seat, but its 5.66% vote share had a measurable impact on the results.Since then, LJP(RV) has moved from being a marginal alliance partner to a more consequential NDA component.It won all five Lok Sabha seats it contested in Bihar in 2024, giving Chirag Paswan a 100% strike rate, and in the 2025 assembly election it contested 29 seats under the NDA arrangement and won 19. The BJP and JD(U) contested 101 seats each, while LJP(RV) secured 29.That progression provides the context for the 403-seat announcement. Chirag Paswan now has five Lok Sabha MPs, 19 MLAs in Bihar and a Union cabinet position. The question is whether that political weight can be extended beyond Bihar.The latest phase of the UP push took shape in September, when Paswan launched his party's youth outreach in Prayagraj. At the "Youth Bole Toh" programme, he spoke about education, employment, skills and greater youth participation in politics, and announced plans for a National Youth Commission.On September 28, he made the electoral plan explicit: "There is no doubt that LJP (Ram Vilas) will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections."The following day, he said the response in Prayagraj had strengthened his confidence in the UP plan. LJP(RV) MP Rajesh Verma subsequently said the party was preparing for all 403 seats, while making clear that the eventual alliance arrangement would be decided later.The 2020 Bihar assembly election was the debut test of Chirag Paswan's leadership. His father, Ram Vilas Paswan , had just died a few days ago.The LJP won only one seat but emerged as a significant factor in 54 constituencies where its vote total was greater than the victory margin. In 25 seats where JD(U) finished second, LJP's vote exceeded the winning margin. Chirag was explicit about the objective, saying after the election: "My main idea in the election was to make the BJP stronger. I am happy with the impact I have had in this election."The BJP finished with 74 seats in that election, ahead of JD(U)'s 43 for the first time. The episode demonstrated that LJP did not need to win seats itself to affect the relative strength of its larger alliance partner.The 2025 Bihar election showed the other side of the equation. LJP(RV) was no longer operating as a spoiler outside the alliance. It contested 29 seats as an NDA partner and won 19, converting its electoral relevance into representation inside the alliance.UP could now test both models: LJP(RV) as an alliance partner with an electoral base of its own, and LJP(RV) as a potential vote-splitter in constituencies where even a few thousand votes can decide the outcome.The potential constituency is significant, but far from straightforward.The BSP won no seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha election in UP and polled around 9.4%. At the same time, the SP expanded its support among Dalit voters as part of its broader PDA coalition. A Lokniti-CSDS post-poll analysis showed a sharp difference between Jatav and non-Jatav Dalit voting patterns, with the BSP retaining much stronger support among Jatavs than among non-Jatav Dalits.For Chirag Paswan, the challenge is therefore larger than taking the Paswan identity from Bihar to UP. Pasis, Valmikis, Khatiks and other non-Jatav communities have distinct political histories and local calculations. Whether LJP(RV) can persuade sections of these voters that it is a credible political vehicle will determine whether its UP expansion produces votes or merely an organisational footprint.The impact could also vary by constituency. A modest LJP(RV) vote could matter in a close BJP-SP contest if it draws disproportionately from one side's potential support base. But unlike Bihar in 2020, there is no single obvious target. The BJP, SP, BSP and Congress have overlapping social coalitions, making the direction of any vote transfer harder to predict.The UP expansion also fits Paswan's attempt to establish LJP(RV) beyond its Bihar base. The party has already demonstrated that it can operate outside the state: in the 2023 Nagaland assembly election, it contested 16 seats, won two and finished runner-up in eight, securing more than 8.6% of the vote.But UP is on a different scale. A credible organisation here would give Chiag Paswan a political presence in the country's largest state and potentially strengthen his position in future NDA negotiations.His recent conduct suggests that maintaining an independent identity is part of that calculation. He has criticised the Bihar government's handling of law and order while remaining part of the NDA, and questioned the Election Commission over concerns surrounding SIR before welcoming its subsequent clarification.The UP experiment, therefore, would not simply be about how many seats LJP(RV) could win. It would be abot whether Chirag Paswan can build an influence outside Bihar to make his party a more consequential NDA partner, while retaining the political independence he summed up in his own words: "I am in the alliance but I am not the BJP."
Article Summary: LJP (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan is set to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. The party is preparing for all 403 seats, while leaving open whether it will eventually contest alone or as part of an alliance.

Article Title: SIR row: Will annul Election Commission orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
‘Decisions must be unanimous or by majority’, says Supreme Court

CEC, ECs need to either rebut or endorse allegations about ‘unilateral decisions’

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday asked the Election Commission , CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to clarify whether crucial decisions regarding the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls were taken unilaterally by the CEC, and said it would injunct (bar) those decisions by the three-member commission which were neither unanimous nor by majority.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said irrespective of powers vested in the CEC, the law clearly mandates that all decisions must either be by unanimity or by majority among the three members of the EC. “If we come across instances (where CEC has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,” it said.The statement came after senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, strongly argued for an interim direction to the EC to only take decisions by unanimity during pendency of the petition as the amended CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, gave the CEC enormous powers.The PIL has sought scrutiny of the validity of SIR decisions and ”alterations” in Form 6 for new voters. Singh said since the court could not undo elections, a direction must be issued that in the interregnum, EC must follow the statutory mandate. He pleaded that EC be directed to preserve all records on SIR decisions and Form 6 alteration and produce them before SC for scrutiny.Let us have some authenticated facts before us through their responses.They must respond in a clear and transparent manner. If the records show some of the decisions are not taken by majority, we will injunct those. But we cannot put the cart before the horse, the bench said while also issuing notices to the Centre, deputy EC Manish Garg and EC’s director general (IT) Seema Khanna.This has set the stage for the CEC and, more crucially, the two ECs to either endorse or rebut the allegation that important decisions on SIR were taken by Gyanesh Kumar unilaterally and in violation of the law which lays down that the commission’s calls are to be made either unanimously or, failing that, by majority. The allegation, based on a newspaper report, is at the core of the controversy which has reignited opposition to SIR.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, also questioned the validity of Section 16 of the 2023 Act, which provided that “no court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is, or was, a CEC or an election commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function”.He said this was way beyond the immunity enjoyed even by SC judges and especially when it was not extended even to the PM.Justice Bagchi said, “We will examine the expression ‘or was’. Protection while in office is understandable. Such protection (as provided under Section 16) is perhaps only with regard to the President. It is not given to constitutional court judges under Judges Inquiry Act.”Singh pleaded for suspension of the CEC or divesting him of his authority. When the bench asked who would conduct elections, Singh said the other two ECs would do it. He said in the interim, the SC-mandated selection panel for CEC should be brought back in which the CJI is included along with the PM and the LoP. The 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union minister nominated by the PM.When the bench declined, Singh said the situation was so grave that it could undermine the very basis of our democracy. “Today, the CEC is acting in a manner which is contrary to the statute under which he is appointed. Court should pass some interim orders (restraining the CEC from discharging his functions), otherwise the country will burn,” he said.Patna-based petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh has sought a direction to EC to “produce before SC the complete original and primary records relating to the matters pleaded herein, including minutes, agendas, approvals, file notings, work allocation and delegation orders, IT-access records, server logs, audit trails and database-change histories concerning the functioning of the commission, ERONet/EClNet, alteration of Form 6 and filing of appeals before the Bengal appellate tribunals”.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asks the Election Commission to clarify whether crucial decisions were taken unilaterally by the CEC. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the law clearly mandates that all decisions must either be by unanimity or by majority among the three members of the EC. “If we come across instances (where CEC has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,” it said.

NEW DELHI: The new Congress team in Uttar Pradesh has a daunting challenge at hand: to revive the fortunes of the grand-old-party in the 2027 assembly elections. But before the big political test early next year, there is a pressing concern at hand: the alliance dynamics. And to that extent, the Congress appointments send a mixed signal to ally Samajwadi Party.The appointment of MLA Aradhana Misra-Mona, who is perceived close to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, as the new state chief signals the willingness of the Congress for an amicable seat-sharing discussions. But the simultaneous elevation of Imran Masood, a known critic of Samjawadi Party’s “big brother attitude”, raises obvious questions about the Congress’s intent vis-a-vis its ally.So, how will this contradiction play out when the two parties sit on the table to decide the contours of their alliance? More so, as there is already an open war of words between the leaders of the two parties over the seat share. Congress leaders have insisted that division of seats should be based on “respect and equality.” Aradhana Misra-Mona acknowledges that with the 2027 state elections only a few months away, she would have to hit the ground running as her party seeks to regain political space it has steadily lost in the state since 1989.To understand why Imran Masood’s high-profile appointment may have caused some unease, here’s a look at some of the statements he has made in the recent past.In a video on X Imran Masood said thatClearly, very strong statements which have led to equally strong reactions from the Samajwadi Party. Akhilesh has led the pushback for the Samajwadi Party, making it clear that winnability will be the only criteria for division of seats.When asked about Masood’s remarks, Akhilesh once said: “I have nothing to do with the statement given by anyone. Our INDIA alliance is intact. Those who want to leave the INDIA alliance can go.”Amid reports that the Congress was seeking 150 seats, Samajwadi Party MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel said the grand-old-party should seek seats in proportion to its electoral strength and organisational presence in the state."I think if they are given 50 seats, they should look at their actual position and status before seeking anything more than 50 seats. They should look at their past record. I understand that in Uttar Pradesh, there is no mandate for Congress. If they fight with us, they will benefit. They have only two MLAs in the state. If they fight together, they will benefit."Masood and SP leaders have also engaged in open war of words over who, Rahul or Akhilesh, was more capable of leading the fight against the BJP.While a lot of these remarks are posturing for dominance in seat-sharing talks, the fact is that the open fighting between the two allies has the potential to confuse their cadres. The Congress move to give prominence to Masood could be part of its strategy to keep the pressure going on the Samajwadi Party.However, former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha feels Congress and Samajwadi Party are not in competition. He asserts that Masood’s appointment has a much bigger and important messaging for the minorities, something the Congress should have done long ago.“UP has seen a lot of polarisation under the BJP regime. Muslims form 18% of the state’s population. I think Masood’s appointment is a manifestation of Congress actually beginning to do what it should have done a long time ago, to be bold, to embrace the fact that the minorities are vulnerable under the BJP, that the Muslims need representation, and to stand for them by having a representative who is going to be a working president. The message is very clear that we are not scared, we are not fearful of the majority community treating the Congress or the Samajwadi party, as the BJP likes to call it, as the "Miya" party,” says Sanjay Jha.“I think the more the opposition becomes fearless and embraces secularism and stands up for Muslims who have been targeted in a blatant fashion, is good for politics. So I endorse the political standpoint of the Congress,” Sanjay Jha adds.Masood is a first-time MP and a prominent face in western Uttar Pradesh politics. Ahead of the 2022 UP assembly polls, Masood left the Congress and to join the SP. However, left the SP in October that year and joined the BSP, where Mayawati immediately appointed him coordinator for western UP. In August 2023, however, Mayawati expelled Masood from the party, accusing him of indiscipline and “anti-party activities”. He returned to the Congress later that year.Amid the tussle over seats, Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Dharmendra Yadav has urged Congress leaders to refrain from making public statements on seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and instead raise the issue directly with SP president Akhilesh Yadav.His remarks came a day after Congress' Uttar Pradesh in-charge, Rajendra Pal Gautam, once again called for "equal share and equal respect" for the grand old party in the state.Dharmendra Yadav, Akhilesh Yadav's cousin, described the former chief minister as a "very large-hearted leader." "I would tell my Congress colleagues, wherever they can win, they should not keep that point in front of the media. There is no need to keep it in the media. If they present it in the right way before our leader, then the entire country knows about our leader; he is a very large-hearted leader. But I would tell my Congress colleagues to stop making statements in the media," the Azamgarh MP said.The Congress-Samajwadi Party (SP) alliance won 43 seats in Uttar Pradesh in the 2024 general election, limiting the BJP to 33 in the most populous state. The SP won 37 seats, including the Faizabad Lok Sabha seat that includes Ayodhya, while Congress won six, including Saharanpur, from where Imran Masood was elected.While the Samajwadi Party wants this record to be the guiding principle for alliance talks and winnability to be the sole criterion, the Congress wants a greater share as it feels the SP’s improved performance was due to gains from the alliance. To prove their point, Congress leaders cite SP’s performance in 2014 and 2019 elections, when it could win only 5 seats each.Clearly, both the allies know that they need each other to take on the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. Little wonder then, Rahul and Akhilesh have managed to keep the bonhomie going despite the confrontation between the state leaders. It will be interesting to see how much of a role will Congress give its new working president Imran Masood in the seat-sharing talks.
Article Summary: Imran Masood has been critical of Akhilesh Yadav. Masood's strong remarks have led to equally strong reactions from the Samajwadi Party. There is already an open war of words between the leaders of the two parties over the seat share.

Article Title: In a record, over 10,000 women clear JEE-Advanced

JEE(A): Women accountfor 23% of registrations but 17.8% of qualifiers

NEW DELHI: Women's success rate in JEE-Advanced reached a record high in 2026 despite fewer registrations, with over 10,000 qualifying for the first time during this period. Yet their share of IIT seat allotments barely changed, from 20.15% to 20.22%. Of the top 100 rankers, 97 were allotted seats at just three IITs - Bombay, Delhi and Madras - with Bombay alone taking 68.This time, a total 18,861 admissions were made in IITs, with 20% being female candidates. Among the top 25 rankers, 8 candidates each took admission in IIT Delhi and IIT Madras, while six toppers took admission in IIT Bombay.The Joint Implementation Committee report, prepared by IIT Roorkee, shows sharp gains for SC and ST candidates. Including candidates with disabilities in both years, their qualification rates among registered candidates rose by 9.9 and 8.3 percentage points, respectively, to 50.2% and 42.1%.SC qualifiers increased from 12,528 to 15,856, while the ST count rose from 5,017 to 6,379. Both increases were around 27%, faster than the 4.6% rise in the number of qualifiers, from 54,378 to 56,880.Of 43,112 registered women, 10,107 qualified, taking their success rate to 23.4%, against 21.7% last year.In 2025, 9,404 women qualified from 43,413 registrations. Among women who appeared in both papers, the success rate was 24.9%.Women accounted for 23% of registrations but 17.8% of qualifiers, showing that their improved success rate has yet to close the gap with male candidates.Women received 3,814 seat allotments, up from 3,664, out of 18,861 overall. Their qualifying count grew 7.5%.IITs have added seats exclusively for women to ensure they make up at least one in five new undergraduate students. Their share of allotments is only slightly above that level. The report records 3,777 allotments in seats set aside for women and 37 in seats open to all genders. Women are considered first for women-only seats within the relevant category.The small number allotted seats open to all therefore does not show how many could have secured them on rank alone.The qualifying total also includes students eligible for a one-year preparatory course before starting an IIT degree. Their number rose from 9,644 to 13,127, nearly a quarter of all qualifiers. This route is available to eligible SC and ST candidates and those with disabilities against unfilled reserved seats. Those admitted must pass the course before entering allotted degree programme.Excluding this group, SC and ST qualifiers still increased by about 17% and 19%. However, the overall number qualifying directly for degree programmes fell from 44,734 to 43,753. The report records 189 seat allotments for this course. Qualifying for either of these routes does not guarantee an IIT seat; admission also depends on rank, eligibility and available seats.
Article Summary: Of 43,112 registered women, 10,107 qualified, taking their success rate to 23.4%. In 2025, 9,404 women qualified from 43,413 registrations. Women received 3,814 seat allotments, up from 3,664, out of 18,861 overall.

Article Title: BJP drops all 8 Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha members, including Hardeep Puri - what it means
Article Text:

Cabinet reshuffle on cards?

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday named eight candidates for the Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh, dropping all of its outgoing members from the state. Union petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri and Union minister of state for consumer affairs BL Verma also are among those who have not been renominated.The nominees, approved by the party's Central Election Committee, are Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar. Voting for 10 UP seats is on October 16, and the last date for filing nominations is October 6.The outgoing BJP members, apart from Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma, are Arun Singh, Neeraj Shekhar, Geeta Shakya, Brijlal and Seema Dwivedi.The eighth seat belonged to former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma, who resigned on September 11 after being appointed lieutenant governor (LG) of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. His term was due to end on November 25, like those of the others.Meanwhile, the move has set the ball rolling for different interpretations ahead of the UP assembly polls and the long speculated Union cabinet reshuffle as no sitting BJP member from the state was retained.Puri's name had been widely discussed for renomination, as had that of former Union minister Smriti Irani, who is also absent from the list.It is seen as a move motivated by the 2027 assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, which the party will contest to form government for the third time in the state. The list, inevitably, appears to have names chosen to balance social, regional and caste combinations.The three candidates in the list are from the upper castes, three from Other Backward Classes (OBC) and two from Scheduled Castes. Ojha and Pandey, both Brahmins, are among the upper-caste picks. Dharampal Singh, a Lodhi, replaces outgoing MP BL Verma, who belongs to the same community. The list also spans Pal and Kurmi communities. Two women, Gangwar and Rawat, are among the nominees.The party seems to have leaned towards grassroots and organisational leaders rather than prominent national faces with the induction of Dharampal Singh, an animal husbandry minister in CM Yogi Adityanath 's government.BJP is learnt to have zeroed in on at least 100 MLAs who are reportedly facing anti-incumbency at the ground level and a large number of them may be denied the ticket to contest the UP Assembly elections next year.Sources said this data has emerged after an on-ground assessment done by the party in 255 seats represented by BJP in the UP Assembly.A top UP BJP member confirmed to TOI that about 100 MLAs are on the radar following reports of lack of trust in them among voters. Friction with the organisational brass at the local level is also being accounted for while flagging these legislators, the senior member said. Sources said that feedback has also been taken from RSS vis-à-vis the candidacy of the sitting MLAs.The BJP's decision not to renominate Union petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri and Union minister of state BL Verma has also fuelled speculation that a Union cabinet reshuffle could be on the cards.Under Article 75(5) of the Constitution, a minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament for six consecutive months must cease to hold office. With Puri and Verma's Rajya Sabha terms ending on November 25, their omission from the UP list raises questions over whether the two will be given another route into Parliament or whether the BJP is preparing for a wider reshuffle. The party, however, has not indicated what the move means for either minister.Also beyond Uttar Pradesh, the BJP on Sunday named Dinesh Arya for the Uttarakhand seat and Trinamool Congress (TMC) defector Rukmini "Koel" Mallick for the West Bengal bypoll. In the March round of Rajya Sabha elections, it fielded its unit chiefs in Bihar and Odisha and retained one sitting MP in Odisha.
Article Summary: BJP names eight candidates for the Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh. All of its outgoing members from the state are dropped. Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma also are among those who have not been renominated. Voting for 10 UP seats is on October 16, and the last date for filing nominations is October 6.

Article Title: ‘Unacceptable’: India reacts after Russian strike injures Indian sailor on Black Sea ship

India on Monday condemned the attack on a civilian commercial vessel in the Black Sea as “completely unacceptable” after a Russian drone strike reportedly killed two foreign nationals and injured crew members, including an Indian sailor.The vessel, MV ROYAD MAMMADOV, was attacked outside Romania's territorial waters, according to reports. Article Title: Delhi court grants bail to 17 students, journalists arrested during CEC protest
Article Text:
Delhi Police accused of misconduct with female journalist at Jantar Mantar..

Court sets bail conditions for accused

Police seek custody, defence cites right to protest

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Monday night granted bail to 17 students and freelance journalists arrested during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, and directed jail authorities to ensure medical treatment for those who sustained injuries.In four separate orders passed between 9 pm and 9:25 pm, Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Animesh Kumar of Patiala House Court ordered the release of all 17 accused in connection with an FIR registered at Parliament Street police station.The court directed that the accused be released on furnishing a personal bond with one surety of the like amount. It also said they should be released immediately if their custody was not required in any other case.The court specifically directed the jail superintendent to ensure necessary medical treatment for accused who had sustained injuries, as advised by the medical officer.The accused have been directed not to directly or indirectly induce, threaten or influence anyone acquainted with the facts of the case or tamper with evidence. They have also been restrained from committing any offence while on bail.They must provide their correct permanent and residential addresses and active mobile numbers, keep the numbers operational and inform the court of any change in address.They are also required to appear before the concerned court on every date of hearing and cannot leave the country without prior permission.The court said the investigating agency would be free to seek cancellation of bail if any of the conditions were violated.The FIR was registered under Sections 223(a), 221, 132, 190, 191(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Section 3 of the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act.Police alleged that the accused were part of an unlawful assembly, obstructed or blocked public space, manhandled police personnel and damaged public property.The investigating officer had sought 14 days of judicial custody, arguing that the accused could commit further offences or interfere with the investigation.The defence opposed the plea, arguing that the accused were young and that several were students exercising their democratic right to dissent and protest. Defence counsel also submitted that no individual role had been specified against the accused in the grounds of arrest.The defence pointed out that while police claimed around 50 people were protesting, only 17 had been arrested. It also argued that no CCTV footage of the alleged incident had been produced before the court.The defence further submitted that some of the accused had sustained injuries and their medical examinations had not been conducted immediately after the incident.The court observed that the allegations were serious and noted that a police official had allegedly sustained injuries. However, it said the right to protest peacefully could not be disputed, while assaulting police officials on duty was a serious concern.The court also noted that, except for the offence under Section 132 of the BNS, the offences invoked were bailable in nature. It further observed that the accused did not appear to be habitual offenders and had their entire careers ahead of them.Considering the facts and circumstances, the court ordered their release on bail subject to the specified conditions.The court directed that the accused be produced before the concerned court on October 6 and ordered that a copy of the bail order be supplied to the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, for information and necessary compliance.
Article Summary: A Delhi court on Monday night granted bail to 17 students and freelance journalists arrested during a protest. The court directed jail authorities to ensure medical treatment for those who sustained injuries. The accused have been directed not to directly or indirectly induce, threaten or influence anyone acquainted with the facts of the case or tamper with evidence.

Article Title: National Commission for Women seeks gender-neutral childcare leave, shared caregiving by parents
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Noting that “motherhood should not become a career penalty”, National Commission for Women (NCW) has called for measures to prevent recruitment discrimination against women arising from maternity, as part of a slew of recommendations to govt on laws related to maternity and childcare.In a report — containing 37 recommendations — NCW has also called for a shift to shared caregiving by transforming existing women-centric child care legal framework into gender-neutral child care leave, available to either parent. The commission batted for extension of “gender neutral” child care leave to private sector, mandatory paid paternity leave, expanding childcare leave eligibility to include third child through graded model, and highlighted the urgent need to make room for 5 lakh creches by 2030.It called for maternity protection to reach women beyond the formal workforce, and recommended extending maternity and childcare benefits to informal, gig and platform workers, noting that over 90% of women workers remain outside effective coverage.NCW has submitted its recommendations to the department of personnel and training (DoPT) and women and child development and labour and employment ministries, with a focus on strengthening India’s maternity and childcare framework through shared parenting, universal maternity protection and family-friendly workplaces.It further recommended parity in maternity benefits for biological, adoptive and commissioning mothers, including increasing leave for adoptive and commissioning mothers from 12 weeks to 26 weeks. It also called for amending Section 60(4) of Social Security Code, 2020, in light of the Supreme Court ruling concerning adoptive mothers, while advocating for a child-centric caregiving framework rather than distinctions based solely on biological motherhood.NCW proposed dividing the existing 730-day child care leave structure equally between both working parents, with 365 days each, or allowing a common pool where both parents work in the same organisation. For children aged 0–2 years, it further proposes a 60:40 shared-care model between primary and secondary caregivers.The commission has also proposed extending child care leave to private-sector employees through a phased implementation model, beginning with large industries and subsequently covering medium and small enterprises.
Article Summary: National Commission for Women (NCW) has called for measures to prevent recruitment discrimination against women arising from maternity. NCW has also called for a shift to shared caregiving by transforming existing women-centric child care legal framework into gender-neutral child care leave, available to either parent.

Article Title: Visa doesn't create absolute right to enter India, says Delhi High Court
Article Text:
File photo

NEW DELHI: Delhi High Court has stressed that a foreign national does not have an inherent or legally enforceable right to seek entry into India even if granted a visa. It added the statutory framework does not treat the possession of a visa as creating an absolute and unconditional right of admission into India.Justice Amit Mahajan observed: "The statutory scheme expressly contemplates circumstances in which, notwithstanding possession of requisite travel documents, a foreigner may not be permitted to enter India on grounds, including considerations relating to national security, sovereignty and integrity of India, relations with a foreign State and public health, besides others specified by central govt.""The claim is destined to fail because there is no inherent or legally enforceable right of a foreign national to seek entry," he added. High Court's observations came while dismissing a plea by a Turkmenistan woman, seeking a direction to Centre to furnish a written speaking order giving the reasons for refusing her entry on March 25.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court says a foreign national does not have an inherent or legally enforceable right to seek entry into India. High Court's observations came while dismissing a plea by a Turkmenistan woman, seeking a direction to Centre to furnish a written speaking order giving the reasons for refusing her entry.

Article Title: Only 15% going to work use public transport: NSO
Article Text:
Walking is the 2nd most common mode of work commute

28.3% of people reach workplace on foot: NSO

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Long traffic snarls, a common feature on roads across the country, may be linked to how people commute to work. Only 15% of workers use public transport such as buses, trains, trams or auto-rickshaws, while 46% rely on two-wheelers or cars, according to the first-ever National Household Travel Survey (NHTS) by the National Statistics Office (NSO).Two-wheelers account for 43% of workers' commute nationally and cars for 3%. In urban areas, reliance on these vehicles is higher, with 53% of workers using two-wheelers and 5.7% travelling by car.Walking is the second most common mode of work commute in the country, accounting for 28.3% of workers, 10.7% use bicycles. More than a third of rural workers (36%) walk to work, compared with just 14% in urban areas, as per the data. The survey was conducted between July 2025 and June 2026 and included trips which are longer than 1 km. Travelling to and fro has been counted as two trips in the survey.The survey showed a worker takes an average of 25 minutes to reach the workplace. In urban areas, the commute takes 27 minutes, compared with 23 minutes in rural areas. The morning commute remains heavily concentrated before 10 am, with nearly 95% of workers leaving home for work then.In terms of cost, workers spend an average of Rs 785 a month on commuting, with men spending substantially more (Rs 835) than women (Rs 533). The gap widens further in rural areas, where men spend more than twice as much as women — Rs 674 against Rs 307.In contrast, student mobility shows a markedly different pattern. Walking is the single largest mode, accounting for 37% of students travelling to educational institutions, followed by buses at 29.5% and bicycles at 15.8%. Around 88% reach their institutions within 30 minutes, while the average journey takes 23 minutes. Nearly four in five students leave for school between 7 am and 10 am.Besides meeting the railway ministry’s specific data requirements, the survey is expected to provide insights into how, when and why people travel. “Information on travel patterns and public transport use will help identify gaps in existing transport systems, assess accessibility, optimise routes and improve service frequency and scheduling,” said NSO in a statement.
Article Summary: Only 15% of workers use public transport such as buses, trains, trams or auto- rickshaws. More than a third of rural workers (36%) walk to work, compared with just 14% in urban areas. Workers spend an average of Rs 785 a month on commuting.

Last year, a Hamas team visited JeM's headquarters in Bahawalpur besides a Pak army facility.Senior Hamas functionaries gave a speech in Rawalkote, PoK, on "Kashmir Solidarity Day" last Feb. The gathering was organised under the banner of Al Aqsa Floods, a reference to the mosque in Jerusalem, claimed by both Jews and Muslims.Kasuri, the LeT deputy chief, has been actively participating in public gatherings post-Pahalgam to raise funds and recruit youth. The visuals uploaded by pro-Lashkar accounts on Telegram show him under the protection of armed guards and uniformed men at all these gatherings. In March, Kasuri said that Pakistan would never accept the Abraham Accords and at a rally in Lahore at the end of May said he had become more famous since the attack in Kashmir last year.
Article Summary: designated terrorist Saifullah Kasuri said the Pakistan army would defend Saudi holy sites and 'erase Israel from the world map' Kasuri sought to incite public sentiment by projecting the Pakistani military as an active player in regional conflicts.
