NEW DELHI: Union law ministry Monday notified appointment of three judges for Supreme Court, taking the total strength of the apex court to 37 judges, including Chief Justice of India , against a sanctioned strength of 38 judges. The new judges will take oath of office likely Tuesday.The three new judges for SC are Justice Sunita Agarwal, currently Chief Justice of Gujarat High Court; Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, Chief Justice of Delhi High Court; and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh, Chief Justice of Telangana High Court.The three chief justices were recommended for elevation to the apex court on Sept 28 by the SC collegium, comprising of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Vikram Nath, B V Nagarathna, M M Sundresh and P S Narasimha.Justice Agarwal will be the third woman judge in SC with Justices B V Nagarathna and V Mohana, the other two currently on the bench. While Justices Agarwal and Upadhyay come from the same parent HC of Allahabad, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh's parent HC is Jharkhand.With the latest appointments, Allahabad High Court has four representations on SC bench, the others include Justices Vikram Nath, who will be the next CJI in Feb, and Justice Manoj Mishra.Justice Agarwal and Justice Upadhyay were appointed judges of Allahabad HC in Nov 2011 while Justice Singh was appointed judge of Jharkhand HC in Jan 2012. Justice Agarwal became CJ of Gujarat HC in July 2023. Justice Upadhyay was appointed CJ of Bombay HC on July 29, 2023 and then CJ of Delhi HC on Jan 21, 2025.The law ministry also notified appointment of Saket court judicial officer Gurvinder Pal Singh as additional judge of Delhi HC, a two year tenure before an additional judge is confirmed as permanent judge of the HC.
Article Summary: The new judges will take oath of office likely Tuesday. Justice Sunita Agarwal will be the third woman judge in SC with Justices B V Nagarathna and V Mohana. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh is Chief Justice of Telangana High Court.

Article Title: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on sitting SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's criticism of deletion of a large number of voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) process, when the issue is pending adjudication before Supreme Court , drew a sharp reaction from former CJI BR Gavai, who termed it judicial impropriety.The former CJI refrained from directly commenting on his former colleague's remarks, but stressed a sitting or retired judge of Supreme Court, high court or any court must not speak on matters that are pending adjudication before a court."I am of the firm view that judicial discipline and propriety do not allow any sitting or retired judge to speak something which pertains to issues pending adjudication before SC, HC or any court," Justice Gavai said when asked by the media about Justice Bhuyan's statement at Nalsar, Hyderabad Sunday on the SIR of electoral rolls.Besides Justice Bhuyan, former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman also criticised the intensive revision of rolls, saying a citizen's right to vote, which is at the heart of democracy, was at "great peril" because of "illegal knocking out" of people from voters' lists.The SIR exercise in West Bengal was challenged before SC, which upheld it after tweaking the process by first engaging judicial officers in the scrutiny of documents and then providing for a special appeal provision by constituting tribunals.However, petitions which challenge SIR in different states, where large-scale deletion of voters from draft rolls has taken place mainly because of "logical discrepancy" and "voter mapping" issues, are still pending in courts.Justice Bhuyan, speaking at Nalsar, had said that any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens is intrinsically arbitrary as it strikes at the heart of the Constitution.Former CJI Gavai said he does not want to comment on Justice Bhuyan's statement.Justice Bhuyan had said, "Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens making them citizens without voting rights would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of the Constitution.""If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary... No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution."
Article Summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's criticism of deletion of a large number of voters drew a sharp reaction from former CJI BR Gavai, who termed it judicial impropriety. Former CJI refrained from directly commenting on his former colleague's remarks, but stressed a sitting or retired judge of Supreme Court, high court or any court must not speak.

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has issued a notice to DCP, IGI airport, directing that an inquiry into a sexual assault complaint against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad be completed and the report be filed by the next date of hearing, after rejecting Delhi Police 's request for more time.The court of additional chief judicial magistrate Neha Mittal listed the matter for further hearing on Oct 23.The complainant has accused Azad of raping her on the pretext of marriage.Alleging that police failed to register an FIR, she had approached the court seeking a direction for registration of a case against Azad.During earlier proceedings, the court issued a notice to Delhi Police and asked for a status report. NEW DELHI: BJP on Monday did not renominate two Union ministers, Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma, as its Rajya Sabha picks from Uttar Pradesh, rekindling speculation that PM Narendra Modi is looking to reshuffle his council of ministers as vacancies rise.Two other ministers, Ravneet Singh Bittu and George Kurien, were similarly left out of Rajya Sabha nominations in June, leading to their resignation. While these two were state ministers, a position held by Verma as well, Puri is a Cabinet minister holding the crucial portfolio of petroleum and natural gas.His likely exit from the Cabinet after the then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan quit in July following CJP's stir over paper leaks further makes the case of a reshuffle as both are demanding portfolios. Consumer affairs, food and public distribution minister Pralhad Joshi is currently handling the education ministry as an additional charge.A minister since Sep 2017, former diplomat Puri is the lone Sikh face in the council of ministers and had unsuccessfully contested the Lok Sabha election from Amritsar in 2019.Some Union ministers like Pankaj Chaudhary and Harsh Malhotra, now heading BJP’s state units in UP and Delhi respectively, have been given organisation responsibilities in an indication that their continuation in govt is unlikely to continue beyond the expected reshuffle.Puri’s term as Rajya Sabha MP from UP ends in Nov, and rules allow a minister to hold his office for six months without being an MP. Not having much of a political constituency of his own, it remains to be seen if he, like Bittu, will be deployed in the Punjab assembly polls, scheduled to be held along with four other states, including UP, early next year.While the impending Punjab election was cited by some experts as a case for his continuation due to his Sikh background, BJP brass in the end chose to not repeat any of its RS candidates, a practice it had followed in the last round of elections as well.Since taking over as PM in 2014, Modi has gone for an overhaul of his council of ministers before the mid-term in both his earlier stints, giving rise to the prospect of a major rejig as his govt is now well into its third year in its third stint.

Article Title: National Commission for Women issues safety guidelines to step-up monitoring of app-based and digital transport services
Article Text:
The NCW issued guidelines for the safety of women using app-based cabs (representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Taking note of safety concerns emerging from across states the National Commission for Women has issued guidelines to states and UTs for safety of women passengers using app-based and digital transport services calling for appropriate verification of criminal antecedents, police verification and background of drivers before onboarding, monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours and providing SOS buttons in every cab to send out alerts to the command-and-control centre.The NCW notes that as cabs, auto-rickshaws, bike taxis and other app-enabled transport services have become an integral part of everyday mobility, particularly for women travelling independently, ensuring safety throughout the journey has assumed greater importance.Instances relating to mismatch in driver or vehicle identity, route deviation, inappropriate conduct, harassment, stalking, unsafe drop-offs, delays in emergency response and inadequate grievance redressal underline the need for a coordinated and accountable safety framework.The guidelines issued in this backdrop also take into consideration the recommendations of the Justice J S Verma Committee Report, 2013, and the regulatory framework under the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, issued by the ministry of road transport and highways.NCW chairperosn Vijaya Rahatkar, has written to the chief secretaries of all states and UTs, requesting appropriate measures for implementation of the guidelines.Bringing focus on verification of driver and vehicle, the guidelines lay down that the aggregators shall ensure that the driver and vehicle assigned to a passenger match the details displayed on the application. “Any unauthorised change in the driver or vehicle shall be appropriately flagged in the application and treated as a safety concern,” it asserts. The guidelines also call for mechanisms for real-time alerts for route deviations or suspicious stoppages.The guidelines also call for penalty-free cancellation in case of identity mismatch. The guidelines also lay down that the aggregators must strive to maintain a verified pool of women drivers, enabling women travelling alone with the option to request a woman driver through the application.Calling for enhanced verification and monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours, the guidelines set out measures ranging from mandatory driver photo verification at trip commencement, addressing driver intoxication, enhanced command and control centre monitoring and a safe-drop option at the end of the ride.“Aggregators may establish a dedicated and time-bound grievance redressal mechanism for complaints relating to driver misconduct, harassment, assault, route deviation, unauthorised driver or vehicle substitution and failure of emergency-response mechanisms,” the guidelines state.
Article Summary: The National Commission for Women issued guidelines to states and UTs for safety of women passengers using app-based and digital transport services. The guidelines call for appropriate verification of criminal antecedents, police verification and background of drivers before onboarding, monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours and providing SOS buttons in every cab.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir: High court quashes PSA detention of Shopian man for ‘showing anti-national tendencies’

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir high court quashed the preventive detention of a man booked under the Public Safety Act (PSA) on charges of showing a disposition towards anti-national activities, terming the allegations against him “prima facie vague”.The detention of Mashooq Ahmad Shah of Shahlatoo was in violation of constitutional guarantees envisaged under Article 22(5) of the Constitution, Justice Rajnesh Oswal said in his order Saturday, directing his immediate release if he was not wanted in any other case.The Shopian district magistrate on Dec 23, 2025, ordered the detention of Shah based on a police dossier that cited intelligence reports and said that he had “shown a tendency towards anti-national activities in his locality and other parts of the district ... and hatred against the state and govt in order to radicalise and instigate the youth towards anti-national activities”.The dossier further mentioned that Shah “remains a perpetual concern for the security agencies” and “could potentially be used as a conduit by terrorist outfits to build underground networks”. His conduct indicated “he has no respect for judicial proceedings and the law of the land”, it added.Shah was lodged in Jammu’s Kot Bhalwal jail. He moved the HC, arguing that the grounds of detention were false, incorrect, vague and non-existent. The allegations “are illusory and without any material basis”, he said.Justice Oswal concurred with the petitioner that the charges against him were vague and “bereft of necessary particulars”. The court said the state failed to identify the persons and associations with extremist leanings with which it alleged Shah maintained contact, nor did it specify who the youths were with whom the petitioner attempted to establish contact and when.
Article Summary: Mashooq Ahmad Shah of Shahlatoo was booked under the Public Safety Act (PSA) on charges of showing a disposition towards anti-national activities. Shah was lodged in Jammu’s Kot Bhalwal jail. He moved the HC, arguing that the grounds of detention were false, incorrect, vague and non-existent.

Article Title: Two killed, Indian among injured after Russian drone hits Turkish cargo ship
Article Text:
Russian drone strike hits Turkish cargo ship in Black Sea, killing 2 (representative image)

Three Indians among crew, all reported safe

Zelenskyy says captain killed in drone attack

Vessel was headed from Ukraine to Italy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fresh incident involving Indian nationals

NEW DELHI: At least two people were killed and several crew members, including an Indian national, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire aboard a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea.The Indian Embassy in Romania said three Indian nationals were among the crew of the vessel, identified as MV Royad Mammadov, and that one of them was injured and receiving medical attention.“We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea. As per preliminary information, there have been 2 casualties (foreign nationals) while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members,” the embassy said in a post on X.The embassy said it was in close contact with the relevant authorities to establish further details about the safety and welfare of the Indian nationals.Indian ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra spoke to the three Indian crew members who were receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. The embassy said the hospital's chief physician confirmed that all three were in good health and receiving necessary care.“Amb @manojifs spoke with the three Indian nationals receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. He also spoke with the hospital’s Chief Physician, who confirmed that all three are in good health and receiving necessary care. The ambassador assured them of all possible assistance and support,” the mission said.It later said that all three Indian nationals were safe.“We have spoken to them. One of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We are in close touch with the hospital authorities. We are extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members,” the embassy added.The nationalities of the two people killed in the incident were not immediately known.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that two Russian drones had struck a civilian vessel carrying corn in neutral waters.“A horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkiye,” Zelenskyy said.He said Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were aboard the vessel and that the ship's captain had been killed. The fate of another person was still being established, he said.“Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were on board. As of now, unfortunately, we know that the ship’s captain was killed. My condolences. The fate of one other person is still being established,” Zelenskyy said.He added that 11 crew members had been rescued, including one who was injured.Zelenskyy said Ukraine had repeatedly proposed concrete measures to de-escalate the conflict and improve security in the Black Sea.“Pressure is needed to restore global food security. And everyone who is genuinely interested in this must help,” he posted.Romania's interior ministry said its Coast Guard was alerted about the fire at around 11 am local time after the vessel was reported in the country's exclusive economic zone, about 30 nautical miles (55 km) south of Sfantul Gheorghe in Tulcea County.The ministry did not confirm what caused the fire. Romanian media reported that the vessel had been hit by a drone southeast of a Black Sea oil platform, but the reports had not been immediately verified by authorities.Romania's Naval Authority identified the vessel as the Royad Mammadov. According to MarineTraffic, it is a general cargo ship flagged to Saint Kitts and Nevis. It had departed Ukraine's port of Izmail and was headed for Italy.Romanian authorities said 11 crew members had been rescued and two deceased people had been found. Injured crew members were airlifted by helicopter for medical treatment.The Black Sea has faced heightened security concerns amid the Russia-Ukraine war, with attacks affecting commercial shipping and port infrastructure.The incident came a day after a 52-year-old employee of a pharmaceutical warehouse belonging to Indian owners was killed in a Russian strike in Ukraine's Sumy.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday that India had moved beyond advocacy and stepped up efforts in recent months to help resolve the Ukraine conflict by engaging with both Kyiv and Moscow.His remarks came days after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has “good ideas” to find a mutually acceptable solution to the conflict.
Article Summary: Russian drone strike hits Turkish cargo ship in Black Sea, killing 2. Indian Embassy in Romania said three Indian nationals were among the crew of the vessel. Injured crew members airlifted by helicopter for medical treatment. Incident came a day after 52-year-old employee of a pharmaceutical warehouse belonging to Indian owners was killed in Russian strike.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Monday issued an advisory for journalists covering protests, asking them to carry valid identity cards and ensure that their presence or activities do not obstruct police operations or the movement of law enforcement personnel.In a social media post on X, Delhi Police issued the guidelines for journalists and said, "The story matters, so does how you get it!""All journalists assigned to cover protests are advised to carry valid identity cards issued by their respective organisations and/or valid PIB/DIP accreditation cards," the guidelines read."They should keep their identification cards visibly displayed at all times to facilitate identification by law enforcement agencies present at the site. They should also ensure that their presence or activities do not obstruct police operations or the movement of law enforcement personnel," it added."During tense situations, journalists present at the site should maintain a reasonable and safe distance while covering and recording the proceedings. They should position themselves in a manner that clearly distinguishes them from protestors," it further said.This comes days after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment during Saturday's protest against the Election Commission at Jantar Mantar.Delhi Police received the complaints and forwarded them to the Crime Branch for further inquiry.On Sunday, Delhi Police, on its official X handle, said that during the October 3 protest in the New Delhi area, which sparked a "law and order situation", allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. "New Delhi District has received their complaints and the same are transferred to Crime Branch for fair and impartial enquiry."Following the allegations, several independent journalists held a protest outside Parliament Street police station, demanding FIRs against the officers.
Article Summary: Delhi Police issues guidelines for journalists covering protests. It asks them to carry valid identity cards and ensure that their presence or activities do not obstruct police operations or the movement of law enforcement personnel. This comes days after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment.
